speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; to begin my assessment, how many weeks pregnant was your mother when you were born, and was the delivery complicated?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the history of pyloric stenosis in your brother and the bilious vomiting at six hours of life raises concerns for malrotation with volvulus. Given the severity of bilious vomiting in a newborn, I need to confirm if there has been any passage of meconium within the first 24 hours and if the abdomen appears distended. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_X-Ray.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Feeding intolerance, No fever, Vomiting started within first day after birth. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Malrotation with Volvulus. The onset of bilious vomiting within the first 24 hours of life is a surgical emergency; the mention of gastroenteritis is clinically inappropriate for this age and presentation, as it does not cause bilious vomiting or feeding intolerance immediately after birth. Please proceed immediately to the operating room for surgical exploration and Ladd's procedure.
